summary:
Museum of Lost Spacecraft is an interactive 3D digital museum dedicated to preserving the history of humanity’s space exploration.

Our project brings together 15 spacecraft and scientific instruments left behind on the Moon, Mars, asteroids, and in deep space. Through an immersive web experience, users can explore 3D models, discover individual missions, and learn about the technology, scientific achievements, and stories behind each spacecraft.

We address an often-overlooked aspect of space exploration: what happens to spacecraft after their missions end? These machines remain important historical and scientific artifacts, yet their stories are scattered across different sources and are not always accessible to the general public.

By combining interactive 3D visualization, scientific research, and storytelling, we transform forgotten space technology into an engaging digital museum. Our goal is to make space exploration history more accessible, inspire curiosity, and encourage interest in science, engineering, and future space missions.
details:
Museum of Lost Spacecraft is an interactive digital museum that brings attention to spacecraft and scientific equipment left behind during humanity’s exploration of the Moon, Mars, and deep space.

Our project features 15 spacecraft and space exploration objects, presented through an immersive 3D experience. Visitors can explore different sections of the museum, including the Moon, Mars, and the Mission Archive.

Users can rotate 3D models, zoom in, and discover the history, purpose, scientific contributions, and final destinations of individual spacecraft. The archive provides photographs, technical specifications, and historical information about each exhibit.

The main goal of our project is to preserve and share an often-overlooked part of space exploration history. Spacecraft that have completed their missions are not simply abandoned machines: they represent decades of scientific research, engineering achievements, and human curiosity.

Our solution makes this history more accessible through interactive visualization and educational storytelling. Instead of presenting information through traditional articles alone, we allow users to explore spacecraft visually and learn about their missions in an engaging way.

The project combines 3D visualization, historical research, digital storytelling, and web technologies. We use official NASA 3D models for selected exhibits, while other spacecraft are represented through original illustrations created for the project.

We believe this approach can encourage interest in astronomy, engineering, space exploration, and STEM education, particularly among younger audiences.

Our project is designed as an accessible educational experience that connects the history of past space missions with the future of space exploration.
